item.title: 18-Wheeler overturns in north Abilene
item.description: ABILENE, Texas (KTAB/KRBC) - An 18-wheeler rolled over on Tuesday afternoon in north Abilene. The crash occurred around 2 p.m. on March 3 at the intersection of Interstate 20 and U.S. 277. Police said excessive speed caused the driver to lose control, resulting in the truck overturning. No injuries were reported. No further information is [...]

item.title: 325 Day: Supporting Local, Giving Back, and Having Fun
item.description: Abilene Teachers Federal Credit Union launched 325 Day, a day to support local businesses, give back, and have fun, which has grown into a meaningful tradition with increasing participation from businesses and nonprofits in Abilene and the 325-area code.

item.title: Runoff set in Brown County judge race
item.description: BIG COUNTRY, Texas (KTAB/KRBC) - A runoff has been set in Brown County for county judge. Since none of the three candidates received more than 50% of the vote, the top two contenders, Patrick Howard and Tom Munson, will advance to a runoff election. item.title: Abbott projected as GOP nominee for governor; set to face Hinojosa in November
item.description: Incumbent Gov. Greg Abbott is set for a run at a fourth term after winning the GOP nomination on Tuesday, according to Associated Press Projections. On the Democratic side, Texas Rep. Gina Hinojosa, D-Austin, is the projected winner.

item.title: Tom Sell heads to runoff in TX-19 GOP race
item.description: LUBBOCK, Texas -- Tom Sell is heading to a runoff election between either Matt Smith or Abraham Enriquez for Texas' 19th Congressional District, according to results late Tuesday night that were too close to call at the time this article was updated. item.title: Crockett v. Talarico: Texas Democrats battle for a chance at flipping a U.S. Senate seat
item.description: Former colleagues in the Texas House of Representatives face off Tuesday night to see who will represent the Democratic Party in the race for the U.S. Senate. A Democratic candidate has not won a statewide election in Texas in three decades.

item.title: Why Tuesday is likely the first of two primaries for the Texas Republican Senate race
item.description: The 2026 U.S. Senate race in Texas is shaping up to be a highly contested election between Republican Sen. John Cornyn, Texas Attorney General Ken Paxton, and U.S. Rep. Wesley Hunt, with the potential for a runoff between the top two candidates.
